Hi Marta —

Appreciate the data and the heads-up. We can definitely work with you on a short-term price preservation and a prorated credit for the Q1 overage. Proposed outline below (high level):

- Price hold: maintain current effective unit rate on your baseline commit for 60 days post-signature (we can extend to 90 days pending finance sign-off). This covers the transition period while you onboard the uplift.
- Incremental commit pricing: incremental capacity above baseline will be priced at an incremental tier with a one-time uplift discount (proposed 6.5% off incremental units for the first 6 months).
- Overage credit: Redwood will apply a one-time invoice credit equal to 20% of the verified Q1 overage spend (applied on the first invoice after amendment execution). We verified your CSV and will include a short reconciliation step.
- Burst/elastic reserve: offer 25% burst credits (token-based) for the first 90 days to smooth unexpected spikes during ramp.
- Operational notes: credits will appear as a standalone credit line and will not change baseline invoice cadence. Pricing hold is limited to base SKU and baseline commit only.

I'll get internal alignment and follow up with a more formal amendment and a draft we can route to DocuSign. Would you be available for a 30-min sync next Tuesday?

Cheers,
Chloe Martin

Ben / Lauren —

Soltec wants a price hold and a credit for a Q1 overage; they plan to double commit in July. I ran a preliminary offer (see my reply above). Need quick alignment before I send the formal amendment. My recommended package (aim to close within two weeks):

1) Economic concession
   - Price hold: 60 days guaranteed; escalate to 90 days if Finance approves (we should push for 60).
   - Incremental tier discount: 7% at the incremental tier for the first 6 months (sweetener to secure the uplift).
   - Overage credit: one-time credit equal to 20% of verified Q1 overage spend (applied to first post-amend invoice).
   - Burst credits: 25% token credits for 3 months to cover ramp spikes; caps at $30k monetary equivalent.

2) Operational guardrails
   - Proration: credits prorated to the verified overage amount; no forward-looking discounts past the 6-month window unless they convert to a higher committed tier.
   - True-up cadence: standard quarterly true-up; new commit effective from next full billing cycle after DocuSign execution.
   - Invoice treatment: credit shows as credit memo; finance sign-off required for revenue recognition treatment (note: we should avoid multi-period revenue reversal).

3) Negotiation script for calls (short):
   - "We can preserve your current baseline pricing while you ramp, and will apply a one-time credit for the Q1 spike. In return, we need the uplift committed and a 12-month minimum on the new baseline. This lets us offer a meaningful concession without impacting long-term unit economics."

4) Ask list for CS/OPS
   - Run a usage reconciliation and confirm the verified overage figure (attachment from Soltec suggests ~18%).
   - Draft amendment v3 with the above terms; include explicit expiration date for the offer (May 12 end of day).

Please confirm the incremental discount at 7% or push back to 6.5% (I can negotiate within that band). Also need Lauren to route to Finance for quick sign-off on invoice credit accounting — BCC them if needed.

Thanks,
Chloe
